# Exact-candidate release handoff

The repository publisher is `.github/workflows/release.yml`, triggered only by manual dispatch. Pushing a tag alone does not publish. Its selected workflow ref supplies tooling; the separate full source SHA supplies the candidate. The workflow must first exist on the default branch for GitHub to discover manual dispatch. Publication requires a release commit on the actual default branch: either made there directly or the merge from the designated primary development branch into it. The merge itself is the release commit. Publish/read back that default-branch commit before creating its tag; publication requires the existing tag peeled to that exact source and agreement with the canonical manifest version.

The publisher reads the actual default branch from repository metadata and pins its ref, then follows first-parent Git objects before any release mutation and again at final readback. It rejects a revision/development tip reachable only through side history; a later default-branch advance preserves an eligible pinned release. Missing, substituted, cyclic or more than 1,000 first-parent steps of history stop publication without selecting another source. This requires repository Contents read in addition to release write access. The check works with shallow candidate checkouts; no workflow fetch-depth change or caller-supplied branch field is required. Structural ancestry does not establish the human-designated development role or exact commit-body/notes equality: the coordinator verifies those before handoff.

Prepare complete body-only Markdown through [release-message preparation](../.agents/plugins/sdd-manager/skills/sdd-forge/references/release-message.md), using [Git highlights](../.agents/plugins/sdd-manager/skills/sdd-forge/references/release-highlights.md) for changes and verified ancillary inputs. Release documents may be committed inside the active revision directory; record their final paths and move the owned documents during the release commit when needed. Retain campaign plans/reports in their directory. Refresh coverage through the exact release result, including both sides of a development merge; preserve applicable human material and hash the exact UTF-8 final bytes. The direct/default or development-merge release commit carries that same Markdown body, and its tag points to the exact commit. The selected `source`/`notes_source` must identify it. Transfer those bytes as `notes`, not a local filename. Version agreement alone does not establish freshness. Finalized root `RELEASE-NOTES.md` (or the selected final destination) is retained after every outcome; only the separate internal highlights checkpoint may be cleaned after actual published-body readback confirms consumption. A dispatch, build-only run or failed publisher does not consume that checkpoint.

Dispatch one string input named `handoff`, containing this JSON object. Pass it using a structured API/CLI input file, never interpolate notes into shell code.

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | Full lowercase 40-character candidate SHA; publishing requires an eligible release commit on the actual default branch's first-parent history. |
| `tag` | `v` followed by that source’s exact manifest version, including any build metadata. Publisher versions use numeric MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional `-prerelease` and `+build.metadata`; build identifiers are nonempty ASCII letters/digits/hyphens separated by dots. |
| `notes_source` | Same SHA as `source`; editorial coverage must actually reach it. |
| `notes` | Nonempty curated multiline Markdown body, without YAML front matter. |
| `notes_sha256` | SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 `notes` bytes. |
| `publish` | Boolean; false performs build/checks only. |
| `prerelease` | Boolean, explicitly selected. |
| `make_latest` | Boolean; stable latest is opt-in, prohibited for prereleases. |
| `request_id` | Unique 1–80 character correlation marker: letters, digits, underscore or hyphen. |

The complete handoff is limited to 60,000 UTF-8 bytes. Unknown or missing fields are rejected. Oversized notes require an accepted alternative transport before dispatch; no automatic arbitrary URL retrieval is implemented.

The candidate Git root contains source tooling and evidence; the distributable root is `.agents/plugins/sdd-manager/`. The publisher validates that subtree and emits package-relative members under `sdd-manager/`, excluding root repository README/notices and source-only material. The complete package README and LICENSE are retained; disclosure/usage templates ship only in assets/.

The build job runs source support checks and tooling publisher contracts, builds the explicit shipped inventory and verifies every ZIP member against the committed source. Archives retain the selected commit’s timestamps in UTC and source identity while rebasing member names to the package root. The publishing job rebuilds the same candidate and compares its archive hash with the build job before any release call. Build-only performs no tag/release/latest writes. The tag is created separately on the verified candidate when that effect is authorized.

A single repository/tag concurrency group retains running work and queues pending runs within GitHub’s supported bound. Repeated invocations read the complete release/asset inventories. Matching drafts upload only verified missing assets; matching published releases require readback and perform no mutation. Field conflicts, foreign/duplicate/starter assets or differing bytes stop without deletion or clobber. An uncertain mutation exits; inspect actual provider effects before a new invocation. Completed assets remain in a draft until every required asset is verified. After initial inventory discovery or an acknowledged creation, subsequent reads address the exact release ID with complete paginated assets; immediate global inventory visibility is not required. Missing or substituted ID readback stops without recreating or replaying a mutation.

Final verification reads actual tag source, body, state, asset downloads and latest identity. Stable/non-latest publication preserves the observed prior latest identity; a provider discrepancy is reported rather than silently corrected. The log and `build/release-observation.json` record source, workflow commit, run/request identifiers and hashes without credentials. Correlate the actual workflow run and retain its observation/logs as release evidence. Local contract success does not establish CI or hosted publication success.
